name: HTTP Request Tester
blurb: send a request and see headers, timing and the response
intro: In the app, Send makes the request from this page with fetch() and captures status, timing, headers and body; the results explain the status, the caching, CORS and security headers, and whether a browser will preflight it (WHATWG Fetch rules). The same request comes back as curl, fetch and raw HTTP.

inputs.label: URL
inputs.help: https://… for another server (needs CORS), or /api/… for this app.

inputs.label: Send cookies to other origins (credentials: include)
Response (written by Send, or pasted)
inputs.help: Status line, headers, a blank line, the body (curl -i output works). Timing goes on a line '# timing total=412 ttfb=388': a bare number is milliseconds (412ms works too); a value ending in s is seconds, as curl -w prints it (total=0.412s).

examples.title: POST JSON to an echo API (with a captured response)

{"args":{},"data":"{\"device\":\"dev-01\",\"temp_c\":21.5}","json":{"device":"dev-01","temp_c":21.5},"url":"https://httpbin.org/post"}

usage: Give method, url (absolute http(s) or a /path on the app), headers as 'Name: value' lines, an optional body and optionally a captured response (first line '<status> <text>' or 'ERROR <message>', optional '# timing total=<ms> ttfb=<ms>' where a bare number is milliseconds and a value with an s suffix (or curl's time_* names) is seconds as curl -w prints them, header lines, blank line, body - curl -i output also works, with the timing line after the body). It returns request checks (forbidden headers, body on GET, invalid JSON), the CORS preflight prediction, the status with its meaning, timing, body size, header findings (CORS, caching, compression, HSTS) and curl/fetch/raw-HTTP texts. run() sends nothing: agents run the curl text themselves and paste the output into response.
sources: WHATWG Fetch Standard: forbidden request-header names, CORS-safelisted methods/headers, CORS preflight
W3C Resource Timing Level 2 (timing phases, Timing-Allow-Origin)
